MOD=Kun|S=je|O=de naam van het programma|A=nog eens|I=herhalen?
Can you repeat the program's name?
A colleague names a program too quickly for you to catch it. Ask informally to hear its name again.
Nog eens asks for repetition; it does not ask for a different program or a new name.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=het laatste deel van je vraag|NEG=niet|PT=verstaan.
I did not catch the last part of your question.
A colleague has just asked you something. Explain that you could not clearly hear the final part of the question.
Verstaan concerns the spoken wording here. It does not claim that you disagree with the question.
Please repeat the order of the checks.
A formal trainer has listed several checks. Politely ask for the order of those checks to be repeated.
Alstublieft marks polite address. The object is the order of the checks, not an instruction to perform them again.
Did you say that the appointment is tomorrow?
You are unsure whether you heard tomorrow as the appointment date. Ask your colleague to confirm what they said.
Zei is past and should be treated as a past question. Dat de afspraak morgen is reports the content being checked.
The sound sometimes drops out when you speak.
During a remote explanation, some of your colleague's speech disappears. Explain that the sound sometimes drops out while they talk.
Soms makes the symptom intermittent, not constant. Wanneer introduces the circumstance in which it occurs.
Could you repeat the reference number a little more slowly?
A customer has read a reference number too quickly. Address them formally and ask for a slower repetition.
Zou u ... kunnen is a polite request. Wat softens the request for a slower pace.
I cannot hear the last digits clearly.
Someone is reading a number over a poor connection. Explain that the last digits are not coming through clearly.
Niet goed limits hearing quality; it does not mean the digits are incorrect.
T=Bij het tweede cijfer|PAST=onderbrak|S=de verbinding|O=het gesprek.
At the second digit, the connection interrupted the call.
You are explaining an earlier failed exchange of a reference number. Say the call was interrupted at the second digit.
Onderbrak is singular past. Bij het tweede cijfer identifies when the interruption happened.
Let's repeat the instructions one at a time.
A group is confused by several instructions given together. Suggest repeating them separately, one after another.
Één voor één means one at a time. The proposal is to repeat the instructions, not necessarily execute them immediately.
I will write the number down while you repeat it.
A customer is about to repeat a reference number. Tell them formally that you will write it down as they repeat it.
Terwijl marks simultaneous actions. Herhaalt is final inside the subordinate clause with subject u.
Q=Welk woord|AUX=heb|S=je|PP=na de naam van de toepassing|PT=gebruikt?
Which word did you use after the application's name?
A colleague's sentence contained a word you missed immediately after the application name. Ask which word it was.
The question asks about a word in completed speech. Heb ... gebruikt forms the perfect bracket.
After each step I briefly repeat the instruction.
A trainer asks how you keep track of instructions during a demonstration. Explain your routine of briefly repeating each instruction after its step.
Na elke stap is one first constituent; herhaal precedes ik. Kort describes the repetition's brevity.
What does this icon mean in this application?
You see an unfamiliar icon while learning an application. Ask a colleague what it means in that application.
Dit agrees with het pictogram. The question concerns its meaning, not its visual location.
V=Bedoel|S=je|G=dat ik alleen de testgegevens moet verwijderen?
Do you mean that I should delete only the test data?
A colleague gives a deletion instruction during a test. Check that the instruction is restricted to the test data.
Alleen limits the data affected. This is a clarification question, not a completed deletion or permission to delete live data.
I know the abbreviation, but I do not know what it stands for.
A colleague uses an abbreviation you recognise visually. Explain that you recognise it but do not know its meaning.
Kennen expresses familiarity with the abbreviation; weten introduces the factual content in the embedded clause.
Can you explain that concept with a simple example?
A colleague has used a difficult concept. Ask informally for an explanation through a simple example.
Uitleggen remains joined after kunnen. Een eenvoudig voorbeeld has no -e because voorbeeld is an indefinite singular het-word.
S=Ik|V=weet|NEG=niet|G=of dit een waarschuwing of een fout is.
I do not know whether this is a warning or an error.
You see a system message but do not know how to interpret it. Explain that you cannot yet tell whether it is a warning or an error.
The first of means whether, while the second of joins the two possibilities. Neither meaning automatically diagnoses the cause.
Yesterday we understood that term differently.
A team discussion has clarified a term's meaning. Explain that the group interpreted it differently yesterday.
Begrepen here is the plural simple past, not a participle with an omitted auxiliary. Anders describes interpretation.
IM=Noem|O=een concreet voorbeeld van een mislukte aanmelding.
Give a concrete example of a failed sign-in.
During a demonstration, you need a concrete illustration of a failed sign-in. Ask your colleague informally to give one.
Noem requests an example rather than telling the colleague to cause a failure. Mislukte describes an unsuccessful attempt.
A warning is not the same as a disruption.
A new colleague treats every warning as an outage. Explain that a warning and a disruption are different things.
Hetzelfde als is an equality expression negated with niet. The sentence does not claim that warnings are harmless.
Q=Welke betekenis|V=heeft|S=het woord rechten|L=in dit scherm?
What does the word rights mean on this screen?
An unfamiliar screen uses the word rights. Ask a colleague what that word means in that interface.
The subject is het woord rechten; plural-looking rechten is the mentioned word, not the grammatical subject.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=het verschil tussen afsluiten en verwijderen|PT=begrepen.
I have understood the difference between closing and deleting.
A colleague has explained ticket handling. Confirm that you now understand the difference between closing a ticket and deleting it.
Heb begrepen marks achieved understanding. Closing and deleting remain distinct actions, not equivalent alternatives.
G=Als u zegt dat het account nieuw is,|V=bedoelt|S=u|G=dat het pas is aangemaakt?
When you say the account is new, do you mean it was created recently?
A customer calls an account new. Address them formally and clarify whether they mean that it was created recently.
The fronted als-clause is followed by the main finite bedoelt and subject u. New is checked as recent creation, not unfamiliarity.
I understand the term, but I do not yet see a practical example of it.
After an explanation, tell a colleague that the term makes sense but you still need a practical example of it.
Er ... van refers back to the term. Geen negates an indefinite example; understanding a term and seeing an example are distinct.
MOD=Kun|S=je|I=voordoen|G=hoe je een nieuw ticket opent?
Can you demonstrate how you open a new ticket?
You are learning the ticketing tool. Ask a colleague to demonstrate the process of opening a new ticket.
Voordoen asks for a demonstration, not only a verbal explanation. The embedded how-clause ends in opent.
I will follow your example first and then try it myself.
A colleague is about to demonstrate a task. Explain that you will follow the example before attempting it yourself.
Jouw emphasises the demonstrator's example. The shared subject ik also belongs to the second coordinated verb probeer.
Please show me where you open the settings.
You are being trained by someone you address formally. Politely ask them to show where they open the settings.
Me is the viewer. U inside the embedded clause refers to the person demonstrating, not to the learner.
S=Ik|V=ben|O=de stappen uit jouw demonstratie|F=aan het|I=noteren.
I am writing down the steps from your demonstration.
During a colleague's demonstration, explain that you are currently taking down the steps they are showing.
Aan het noteren is ongoing, not completed. Uit jouw demonstratie identifies the source of the steps.
Can I do this exercise in the test environment first?
Before attempting a newly demonstrated task, ask whether you can practise it in the test environment first.
Eerst requests a safe practice stage. It does not imply permission to perform the task in production afterward.
During the demonstration I saw a different menu.
You are comparing your screen with an earlier demonstration. Report that you saw a different menu during the demonstration.
Zag is singular past. Ander means different; the sentence does not assert which menu is correct.
S=Ik|V=begrijp|O=de stap|C=beter|G=als ik die zelf uitvoer.
I understand the step better when I carry it out myself.
A colleague asks how you learn a demonstrated action. Explain that doing the step yourself helps you understand it better.
Die refers to de stap. The subordinate verb uitvoer stays joined at the end; the comparison is about understanding.
Could you demonstrate the same action once more?
You missed part of a trainer's demonstration. Address the trainer formally and ask for the same action to be demonstrated again.
Dezelfde preserves the exact action; it is not a request to demonstrate a different procedure.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=de stappen van de demonstratie|L=in mijn notities|PT=opgeslagen.
I have saved the demonstration's steps in my notes.
After a demonstration, a colleague asks whether you retained the procedure. Say you saved its steps in your notes.
Saved notes do not by themselves prove mastery. Opgeslagen is the irregular separable participle of opslaan.
Let's compare the two screens first.
Your screen looks different from your colleague's demonstration. Suggest comparing the screens before continuing.
Eerst puts comparison before the next action. The proposal does not identify a cause yet.
Q=Welke stap|V=komt|T=na het openen van de instellingen?
Which step comes after opening the settings?
During a demonstration, you lose track immediately after the settings are opened. Ask which action follows that point.
Het openen is a nominalised infinitive naming the activity. Welke stap is the subject of komt.
S=Ik|V=maak|O=een korte checklist|TE=om de demonstratie later te kunnen herhalen.
I am making a short checklist so I can repeat the demonstration later.
A colleague asks why you are making a checklist during training. Explain that it will help you repeat the demonstrated procedure later.
Om te kunnen herhalen expresses purpose and future ability. Checklist is a de-word, so korte takes -e.
Which environment exactly do you mean?
A customer mentions an environment without identifying it. Address them formally and ask which particular environment they mean.
Welke modifies de omgeving. Precies narrows the reference rather than questioning the customer's honesty.
Can you give the full error text?
A colleague has mentioned an error only generally. Ask informally for the complete displayed text, without requesting secret information.
Volledige asks for complete wording, not a guessed summary. Fouttekst is a de-word.
S=Ik|V=heb|NEG=nog niet genoeg|O=informatie over de gewenste wijziging.
I do not yet have enough information about the requested change.
You are asked to act on a change request that lacks detail. Explain that you do not yet have enough information about the requested change.
Nog niet genoeg concerns the amount of information. It does not mean that no information at all has been provided.
S=Ik|V=weet|NEG=niet|G=welk van de twee schermen u bedoelt.
I do not know which of the two screens you mean.
A customer refers to a screen while two are being discussed. Address them formally and explain that the reference is unclear.
Welk refers to singular het scherm, even with van de twee. The embedded question ends in bedoelt.
Include the date with each example as well.
A colleague is collecting examples of a recurring issue. Ask them informally to include the date for each example.
Bij elk voorbeeld is a prepositional phrase, not the direct object. De datum is the thing to provide.
I have requested the missing version information.
A teammate asks what you have done about incomplete request details. Say that you requested the missing version information.
Opgevraagd reports a completed request, not receipt of the information. Ontbrekende describes what is missing.
Which user does your example concern?
A customer gives an example without identifying whose experience it describes. Ask formally which user the example concerns.
Het gaat om is a fixed expression meaning concern/be about; het is not the user being identified.
Did you mean the test environment or the production environment?
You are checking what a colleague meant in an earlier instruction. Ask whether they meant test or production.
Bedoelde checks earlier intended meaning. Of joins alternatives here, rather than introducing an embedded whether-clause.
S=Ik|V=heb|O=vooral de exacte tijd van het probleem|C=nodig.
I particularly need the exact time of the problem.
A colleague offers several kinds of background information. Explain that the exact time of the problem is especially important for your check.
Heb ... nodig expresses need; vooral prioritises this detail without saying other information is useless.
MOD=Zou|S=u|O=de omschrijving|PP=met één concreet geval|I=kunnen aanvullen?
Could you add one concrete case to the description?
A customer's description is too general to investigate. Address them formally and ask them to add one concrete case.
Aanvullen met adds material to the description. Eén asks for one example, not every historical case.
Without the exact time, I cannot find the report again.
A teammate asks why you cannot locate a particular report. Explain that you need its exact time to find it again.
Zonder gives the missing prerequisite. Niet negates ability to locate this report, not willingness to help.
If anything is missing, I ask about it separately.
You are describing how you handle incomplete instructions. Explain that you separately follow up on missing details.
The conditional clause is one first constituent. Navragen splits as vraag ... na; dat refers to the missing detail.
V=Begrijp|S=ik|C=goed|G=dat de wijziging alleen voor nieuwe accounts geldt?
Do I understand correctly that the change applies only to new accounts?
A colleague has described a change. Check that it affects only accounts created recently, rather than all existing accounts.
Alleen restricts the scope to new accounts. Nieuw does not mean merely unfamiliar in this situation.
I will briefly summarise the agreement.
At the end of an explanation, tell your colleague that you will briefly summarise what you have agreed.
Vat ... samen is separable. This announces a summary rather than claiming new agreement has been reached.
S=Ik|V=controleer|G=of ik de juiste volgorde heb genoteerd.
I am checking whether I wrote down the correct order.
After receiving several instructions, explain that you are checking whether your notes have the correct order.
Of means whether. Heb genoteerd is a final perfect verb group; genoteerd heb is also possible in this clause.
MOD=Kun|S=je|I=bevestigen|G=dat ik het juiste account heb gekozen?
Can you confirm that I selected the correct account?
Before proceeding with a request, ask a colleague informally to confirm that you selected the intended account.
Dat introduces what should be confirmed. Confirmation concerns account selection, not permission for every action on it.
I understood your instruction as a proposal.
You may have misunderstood a formally addressed colleague's earlier wording. Explain that you interpreted it as a proposal rather than a firm order.
Als een voorstel describes interpretation. The sentence does not assert that the speaker really intended a proposal.
S=Dat|V=betekent|NEG=niet|G=dat de storing al is opgelost.
That does not mean the disruption has already been resolved.
A colleague treats a temporary improvement as proof of a completed fix. Explain that the improvement does not establish that the disruption is resolved.
Niet negates the inference. Al is opgelost concerns completion; a workaround and a permanent fix remain distinct.
Which step do you think I skipped?
A colleague says you missed part of the procedure. Ask informally which step they think you skipped.
Volgens jou attributes the judgement to the colleague. Heb overgeslagen asks about a completed omission.
Please say so if my summary is not right.
You have summarised a colleague's explanation. Invite them informally to correct you if your summary is inaccurate.
Gerust reassures the listener that correction is welcome. Als gives the condition for speaking up.
A moment ago I was assuming a different agreement.
You have just realised that you and a colleague understood the arrangement differently. Explain your earlier assumption.
Uitgaan van means assume/take as a starting point. Daarnet places that assumption in the recent past.
Let's put the two interpretations side by side.
You and a colleague have understood an instruction differently. Suggest comparing the two interpretations directly.
Naast elkaar leggen is figurative comparison here. The proposal does not decide which interpretation is correct.
Before I continue, I want to briefly summarise the assignment.
You have received several instructions and are about to continue. Say that you want to summarise the assignment first.
The complete voordat-clause is first; wil follows before ik. Doorga stays joined inside the subordinate clause.
S=Uw voorbeeld|V=is|C=duidelijker dan de oorspronkelijke beschrijving.
Your example is clearer than the original description.
A customer has added an example to an unclear report. Address them formally and explain that the example is clearer than the original description.
Duidelijker dan is a comparative. Uw identifies the customer's example; clearer does not necessarily mean complete.
S=Ik|V=leer|O=de Nederlandse termen voor onze hulpmiddelen.
I am learning the Dutch terms for our tools.
A colleague notices you are writing down unfamiliar words. Explain that you are learning the Dutch names for the team's tools.
Nederlandse is an attributive adjective before plural termen. Learning vocabulary does not imply technical unfamiliarity with the tools.
Can you say the technical terms a little more slowly?
You can follow the explanation but the technical terms are spoken too quickly. Ask a colleague informally to say those terms more slowly.
Iets softens the request. Rustiger concerns pace here, not the correctness of the terms.
S=Ik|V=ken|NEG=nog niet|O=alle Nederlandse namen in dit menu.
I do not yet know all the Dutch names in this menu.
You are learning a Dutch interface. Tell a colleague that some menu names are still unfamiliar to you.
Nog niet alle means not all yet, rather than none. The objects are names, not the menu's technical behaviour.
How do you pronounce this application's name?
You recognise an application name in writing but are unsure how to say it. Ask a colleague for its pronunciation.
Spreek ... uit is separable; subject je follows the finite stem, so there is no -t.
I have added the term to my word list.
A colleague asks what you did with a newly explained term. Say you added it to your word list.
Opnemen means include here, not record someone's voice. In mijn woordenlijst names the destination list.
S=Ik|V=gebruik|O=een voorbeeldzin|TE=om de term beter te onthouden.
I use an example sentence to remember the term better.
A teammate asks how you practise new workplace terms. Explain that you use an example sentence to remember each term better.
Om gives the learning purpose. Onthouden means retain/remember, not merely recognise a word visually.
Is this a common expression in Belgium?
You have heard a workplace expression for the first time. Ask whether it is commonly used in Belgium.
Gebruikelijk means customary/common, not automatically required in every workplace. In België gives the regional context.
T=Tijdens mijn vorige gesprek|PAST=zocht|S=ik|PP=naar het juiste woord.
During my previous conversation I was searching for the right word.
A colleague asks why you paused in an earlier conversation. Explain that you were looking for the right word then.
Zoeken naar can describe a mental search for a word. Zocht places it in a particular past conversation.
S=Ik|V=begrijp|O=de uitleg|C=beter|G=als u korte zinnen gebruikt.
I understand the explanation better when you use short sentences.
You are speaking with a trainer you address formally. Explain that shorter sentences help you follow the explanation.
Als describes the condition that improves understanding. It is a request about language support, not an assessment of the trainer's technical skill.
S=Ik|V=voel|R=me|C=zekerder wanneer ik de term hardop oefen.
I feel more confident when I practise the term aloud.
A colleague asks how you build confidence with unfamiliar Dutch terms. Explain that practising a term aloud makes you feel more confident.
Me matches ik in the reflexive feeling expression. Zekerder is a comparison of confidence, not proof of mastery.
We can first describe a difficult concept in ordinary words.
Your group is struggling with a specialist term. Suggest first describing its meaning using ordinary language.
This is an available communication strategy, not a claim that ordinary wording will cover every technical detail.
IM=Verbeter|O=me|C=gerust|G=als ik de verkeerde term gebruik.
Feel free to correct me if I use the wrong term.
You are practising workplace Dutch with a colleague. Invite them informally to correct you when you use a term incorrectly.
Gerust makes correction welcome. Als introduces the condition; gebruik is final in the clause with subject ik.
